svg.data-what: the eye cut through its middle, seen from the side, light entering from the left: cornea, iris, lens, and the three coats of the eyeball

circle.data-what: the vitreous body, the clear jelly filling the eye behind the lens

path.data-what: the aqueous humour, the clear fluid filling the front of the eye between the cornea and the lens
the sclera, the tough white coat of the eye
the choroid, the dark layer of vessels that feeds the retina and absorbs stray light
the retina, the sheet of light-sensitive cells, rods and cones, and the neurons that begin to process the image
the fovea, the small pit at the centre of the macula: the sharpest vision, packed with cones
the cornea, the clear dome at the front: it does most of the focusing
the ciliary body: its muscle changes the lens's shape to focus near or far, and it makes the aqueous humour
the ciliary body: its muscle changes the lens's shape to focus near or far, and it makes the aqueous humour
the lens, clear and elastic, fine-tuning the focus onto the retina
the iris, the coloured ring of muscle that opens and closes the pupil

rect.data-what: the pupil, the opening in the iris through which light enters

path.data-what: the optic nerve, carrying the retina's signals to the brain; where it leaves, the optic disc, there are no photoreceptors: the blind spot
